jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: plant GROWTH sprite sheet for an original cozy 16-bit pixel-art nature-island game.
Primary request: beautifully designed genuine five-stage growth progressions, not five resized copies. Authentic charming farming-game pixel art with the warmth of Stardew Valley, sharp square pixels, hand-crafted stepped outlines, carefully clustered highlights, warm dark-green/brown selective outline and 3-5 shades per material, upper-left sunlight, three-quarter overhead orthographic view.
CRITICAL LAYOUT: exactly 5 equally wide columns and 6 equally tall rows, exactly 30 sprites, on a 5:6 portrait canvas ideally 1280x1536. Each row is ONE species. The five columns show stage 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 of THAT SAME SPECIES from left to right. Preserve each species' visual identity across its row. Fixed physical scale across stages. The first stage is tiny, stage two short, stage three noticeably taller and leafy, stage four structurally developed, stage five full grown. The ground/root point is at horizontal 50% and vertical 88% WITHIN EVERY CELL. Plant grows UPWARDS from this fixed baseline, not from center. Huge empty space above tiny sprouts is correct; do not enlarge early stages to fill their cells. Keep entire plant and all leaves inside its cell with at least 15% horizontal gutter; never cross cell boundaries. No row labels, column labels, numbers, text, grid, border, heading or frames.
TRANSPARENCY: actual alpha-zero empty background everywhere outside the individual pixel plant silhouettes, with absolutely no colored glow, fog, shadow halo, gradients, solid backdrop, fake checkerboard, colored tile, grass tile base or decorative pedestal. Tiny seed/earth marks directly under seed are allowed. Empty surrounding pixels fully transparent. Roots and bases have crisp edges.
Palette: fresh sage and moss greens, gentle butter yellow highlights, caramel stems and trunks, natural restrained colorful accents. Coherent pixel density in all rows. No vectors, no 3D, no soft painting, no blur, no anti-aliased line art.
Detailed rows follow. Five semicolon-separated states in each row correspond to the five columns EXACTLY.
Row 1 oak: half an acorn with a tiny root; tiny two-leaf sprout; thin woody stem with several broad oak leaves; small branching sapling with a modest round canopy; mature stout warm-brown trunk with dense round green crown.
Row 2 birch: tiny seed in a small earth mark; tiny two-leaf sprout; slender brownish stem with sparse delicate leaves; young tree with white bark beginning and thin leafy branches; mature recognizable white trunk with black marks and airy lime-green leafy crown.
Row 3 pine: tiny pine seed and a green point; short tuft of needle seedlings; thin upright trunk with three sparse tiers of needle branches; young conical evergreen with five clear branch layers; mature tall pine with full deep-green tiered canopy.
Row 4 cherry: tiny seed earth mark; short two-leaf sprout; young slender green-leaf sapling; branching small green canopy with pink closed flower buds; mature graceful brown trunk and full soft pink blooming cherry canopy.
Row 5 apple: tiny apple seed earth mark; tiny two-leaf sprout; small woody stem with several oval green leaves; branching young tree with small green crown and a few white-pink flowers; full round apple tree with visible ripe red apples in its green crown.
Row 6 willow: tiny root shoot; short stem with two narrow leaves; slender young tree with sparse outward branches and narrow leaves; young tree with clear drooping branch tips; mature graceful willow with curtains of delicate hanging green leaves.
Trees must look increasingly substantial from left to right, but mature forms fit safely within cells. Tree species remain visibly distinct.

Row 2 raspberry: tiny root shoot; slender shoot with a few small leaves; several thin upright leafy canes; curved leafy canes with little white flowers and green fruit; fuller leafy canes with recognizable red raspberry clusters.
Row 3 hydrangea: tiny rooted green shoot; short shoot with one pair of broad leaves; low multi-layer leafy shrub; bigger shrub with tightly closed pale green flower balls; mature bush with big round lavender and periwinkle blossom clusters.
